headline: A Taiwanese newspaper report says TSMC may reach its 2027 target for 2-nanometre chip capacity a year early because of heavy orders from Nvidia, AMD and Apple.
score_reason: Pool score kept: based on newspaper and analyst estimates that TSMC has not confirmed.
importance_line: Faster 2-nanometre output could shorten the wait for the newest AI and phone chips and favours TSMC's biggest customers, but it rests on supply-chain estimates and analyst forecasts that TSMC itself has not confirmed.
summary: Wccftech, relaying a report by Taiwan's United Daily News (UDN), says TSMC, the Taiwanese chipmaker that makes processors for Nvidia, AMD and Apple, may reach about 120,000 wafers a month of 2-nanometre capacity by the end of 2026, 20% above the earlier estimate of 100,000 and within the 110,000 to 140,000 range projected for the end of 2027, on orders from Nvidia, AMD, Apple and Qualcomm. Separately, Bank of America expects 2-nanometre chips to rise from 3% to 11% of TSMC's third-quarter revenue, ahead of TSMC's earnings; all of these are estimates, not company figures.
notes: Credit goes to UDN as the first reporter named in the Wccftech text; the link is the Wccftech page where it was read.
